basic_details.job_title: IISER BPR Junior Research Fellow Recruitment 2026 – Apply Online
basic_details.short_information: The Department of Earth & Environmental Sciences at IISER Berhampur has advertised one temporary Junior Research Fellow (JRF) post in a BRNS-funded project, paying ₹ 37,000 + HRA as applicable per month for 1 year, extendable for up to 3 years. An M.Sc. in Geology/Applied Geology/Geological Science with a valid NET/GATE/UGC-JRF/CSIR-JRF/NET-LS qualification is required. Applications go by email to the Principal Investigator, Dr. Tushar M. Chakraborti, so that they reach him by 5:00 PM on Saturday, 21 November 2026.

important_dates.interview_date: To be informed later to shortlisted candidates through email

how_to_apply: Applications are sent by email to the Principal Investigator at [email protected]. The CV and all supporting documents go in a single pdf file of less than 10 MB, with a brief mention of research experience. The subject line must read: “Application for the Position of Junior Research Fellow against advt. no. IISERBPR/EES/BRNS/051026/3758/103/JRF dated 06-11-2026”. The email must be sent by 5:00 PM on Saturday, 21 November 2026. For any information, candidates may contact the PI by email.

A brief mention of research experience

content_sections.heading: IISER BPR Junior Research Fellow (JRF) at a Glance
content_sections.text: The official notification does not specify the age limit or the application fee.

rows.details: Indian Institute of Science Education and Research Berhampur (IISER BPR)
Study on hydrothermal process and its bearing on uranium mineralization in Sarangapalli and Tangeda area, Palnad Sub-Basin, Cuddapah Basin, Palnadu district, Andhra Pradesh
1 year from the date of joining, extendable up to 3 years

content_sections.heading: About the Project
content_sections.text: IISER Berhampur is an Institute of National Importance under the Ministry of Education, Government of India, at Laudigam, Konisi, Berhampur, Ganjam, Odisha. The post is in IISER BPR project no. IISERBPR/EES/BRNS/051026/3758/103, funded by BRNS. The Principal Investigator is Dr. Tushar M. Chakraborti, Assistant Professor, Dept. of Earth & Environmental Sciences (EES). The notice is issued by the Office of Dean, Research & Development.

content_sections.heading: Who Can Apply
content_sections.text: The notice prints the qualification for the one JRF post as follows: M.Sc. or equivalent Degree in Geology/Applied Geology/Geological Science with a minimum of 60% marks or CGPA/CPI of 7.0 on a 10-point scale. Qualification in a National level examination like the National Eligibility Test (NET)/GATE/UGC-JRF/CSIR-JRF/NET-LS. The certificate/fellowship must be valid at the time of admission. Candidates should check the official notification for the discipline-specific eligibility of the post.

content_sections.heading: Pay and Tenure
content_sections.text: The remuneration is ₹ 37,000 per month plus HRA as applicable. The type of engagement is temporary. The period of engagement is 1 year from the date of joining. It is extendable based on progress, performance and availability of funds, for up to 3 years.

content_sections.heading: IISER BPR Junior Research Fellow (JRF) Job Description
content_sections.text: The notice lists the job requirement as: Fieldwork Sample collection and preparation Petrological-mineralogical-geochemical study of samples using Optical microscopes, FE-SEM, XRD, XRF, EPMA and Fluid inclusion micro-thermometry Interpretation of generated data

content_sections.heading: How to Apply for IISER BPR Junior Research Fellow (JRF)
content_sections.text: Applications are sent by email to the Principal Investigator at [email protected] . The CV and all supporting documents go in a single pdf file of less than 10 MB, with a brief mention of research experience. The subject line must read: “Application for the Position of Junior Research Fellow against advt. no. IISERBPR/EES/BRNS/051026/3758/103/JRF dated 06-11-2026”. The email must be sent by 5:00 PM on Saturday, 21 November 2026. For any information, candidates may contact the PI by email. content_sections.heading: Selection and Interview
content_sections.text: The notice says the date and mode of the interview will be informed later to the shortlisted candidates through email. It does not describe the shortlisting method or any other stage.

faq.question: Q1. How many Junior Research Fellow posts has IISER Berhampur advertised?
faq.answer: One post. The notice lists the number of positions as 01, and the type of engagement is temporary.

faq.question: Q2. What is the last date to apply for the IISER BPR JRF post?
faq.answer: The last date is 5:00 PM on Saturday, 21 November 2026. Applications are sent by email to the Principal Investigator.

faq.question: Q3. What is the qualification for the IISER BPR JRF post?
faq.answer: An M.Sc. or equivalent Degree in Geology/Applied Geology/Geological Science with a minimum of 60% marks or CGPA/CPI of 7.0 on a 10-point scale. A NET/GATE/UGC-JRF/CSIR-JRF/NET-LS qualification valid at the time of admission is also required.

faq.question: Q4. What is the salary of the IISER BPR JRF?
faq.answer: The remuneration is ₹ 37,000 per month plus HRA as applicable.

faq.question: Q5. Is HRA paid on top of the ₹ 37,000 JRF pay?
faq.answer: Yes, the notice prints the remuneration as ₹ 37,000 + HRA as applicable. It gives no other allowance.

faq.question: Q6. How do I apply for the IISER BPR JRF post?
faq.answer: Email the CV and supporting documents as a single pdf (less than 10 MB) to [email protected]. Include a brief mention of research experience and use the subject line given in the notice.

faq.question: Q7. What should I write in the email subject line?
faq.answer: Write “Application for the Position of Junior Research Fellow against advt. no. IISERBPR/EES/BRNS/051026/3758/103/JRF dated 06-11-2026”.

faq.question: Q8. How will candidates be selected for the IISER BPR JRF post?
faq.answer: Shortlisted candidates will be informed of the interview date and mode through email. The notice gives no further selection details.

faq.question: Q9. How long is the IISER BPR JRF engagement?
faq.answer: The engagement is temporary for 1 year from the date of joining. It is extendable based on progress, performance and availability of funds, for up to 3 years.

faq.question: Q10. Which project is the JRF post attached to?
faq.answer: It is attached to the BRNS-funded project on hydrothermal process and its bearing on uranium mineralization in Sarangapalli and Tangeda area, Palnad Sub-Basin, Cuddapah Basin, Palnadu district, Andhra Pradesh.
